content.text:
Give Rae a heads-up before it's time to go, not a surprise ending. At two, big feelings still outrun the words to handle disappointment, so an abrupt exit tips her over fast.

A couple of things that tend to help:

- A five-minute and two-minute warning ("two more slides, then we go").
- A small closing ritual — wave bye to the swings, count steps to the gate — so leaving feels like part of the fun, not the end of it.
- Let her "choose" the last thing (slide or swing) so she has a say in how it ends.

Most toddlers still have some protest even with warnings — that's normal at this age and tends to ease as she gets more practice with transitions.
